skill.name: regulatory-affairs-head
skill.description: Regulatory affairs guidance for HealthTech and MedTech teams planning FDA, EU MDR, and global medical device submissions.
skill.summary: Plan medical device regulatory strategy, submission work, and compliance tracking.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The audit confirmed one filesystem side effect in scripts/regulatory_tracker.py, where submission data is written to a local JSON file. The remaining static findings are false positives from regulatory prose, Markdown code fences, and inline file names. No prompt injection, network access, external command execution, or exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Local tracker script can overwrite the configured submissions data file.
remediation.suggestion: Constrain the data file to a documented skill data path, and warn before overwriting an existing file.

content.value_statement: MedTech teams need clear regulatory pathways and submission plans. This skill structures FDA, EU MDR, and compliance work into practical regulatory guidance.
actual_capabilities: Guides FDA pathway planning for 510(k), PMA, De Novo, SaMD, and quality system topics.
Explains EU MDR classification, conformity assessment routes, technical documentation, and submission timelines.
Provides a regulatory decision framework for impact assessment, stakeholder alignment, implementation, and monitoring.
Supports submission status tracking through a local Python tracker script.
Helps define regulatory KPIs, risk mitigation steps, and cross-functional coordination practices.
limitations: It does not replace legal advice or formal regulatory authority feedback.
It does not provide live updates from FDA, EU, or notified body sources.
Several referenced companion guides and folders are not present in the package.
The tracker script stores data locally and does not include access controls.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Submission Pathway
use_cases.description: Compare likely FDA or EU MDR pathways and list key evidence, quality, and timeline needs.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Cross-Functional Readiness
use_cases.description: Turn regulatory milestones into team responsibilities, review checkpoints, and escalation topics.

use_cases.title: Track Submission Status
use_cases.description: Use the local tracker concept to monitor active submissions, overdue items, and authority review status.

prompt_templates.title: Identify a Regulatory Pathway
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new device concept.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me identify likely regulatory pathways for a medical device. Device type: [describe device]. Market: [US or EU]. Risk level: [known or unknown].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Submission Checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate preparation for a planned submission.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a submission preparation checklist for [510(k), PMA, De Novo, or EU MDR]. Include evidence, quality system, labeling, and review milestones.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Regulatory Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess regulatory risks for this product plan: [summary]. Include market access impact, timeline risk, evidence gaps, mitigations, and decision points.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Global Submission Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced coordination across markets and teams.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a global regulatory strategy for [product]. Compare FDA and EU MDR needs, sequence submissions, define responsibilities, and propose KPIs.

output_examples.input: Plan a 510(k) readiness review for a connected patient monitoring device.
output: Recommended pathway: Traditional 510(k), pending predicate confirmation.
Core evidence: performance testing, software documentation, cybersecurity risk management, labeling, and quality system readiness.
Next actions: confirm predicate, schedule a Q-Sub if uncertainty remains, and assign owners for evidence gaps.

output_examples.input: Summarize EU MDR preparation needs for a Class IIa device.
output: Class IIa devices usually require notified body involvement and technical documentation review.
Preparation should cover clinical evidence, risk management, UDI planning, QMS readiness, and post-market surveillance.
Timeline risk is highest when clinical evidence or notified body engagement starts late.

output_examples.input: Create KPIs for a regulatory affairs team managing active submissions.
output: Track submission approval rate, review cycle time, authority question response time, overdue actions, and market access progress.
Review metrics monthly with regulatory, quality, clinical, product, and executive stakeholders.

best_practices: Provide device type, intended use, market, risk class, and current evidence status in each request.
Ask for assumptions and evidence gaps so the output can support regulatory decision making.
Verify final plans against current authority guidance and qualified regulatory counsel.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the output as an official regulatory determination.
Do not omit device risk, intended use, or target market details from planning prompts.
Do not rely on the bundled references for current legal deadlines without checking primary sources.

faq.question: What regulatory regions does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It includes FDA and EU MDR guidance, plus general global regulatory planning concepts.

faq.question: Can it choose the final pathway for my device?
faq.answer: It can suggest likely pathways and assumptions, but final decisions require qualified regulatory review.

faq.question: Does it include live regulatory updates?
faq.answer: No. You should verify dates, forms, and guidance against official regulatory sources.

faq.question: Can it help with software as a medical device?
faq.answer: Yes. The FDA guide includes SaMD considerations such as software documentation, cybersecurity, and lifecycle controls.

faq.question: Does it run external commands?
faq.answer: No external command execution was found in the reviewed skill content.

faq.question: What data does the tracker script store?
faq.answer: The tracker stores submission status details in a local JSON file when used.
